beats.text: This is a seven joint Franka arm in Isaac Sim. Its position controllers are switched off: we command raw motor torques.
First, zero torque. That is pure forward dynamics: the simulator solves the equation of motion, and gravity pulls the arm down.
Now we ask the simulator for g of q, the gravity term, and apply exactly that.
Nothing holds the joint angles, yet the arm floats. The shoulder needs about thirty four newton metres just to hold itself up.
Finally, full inverse dynamics. We want a wave on four joints, so every step we compute mass matrix times acceleration, plus Coriolis, plus gravity.
The shoulder torque is almost all gravity.
The base joint spins about a vertical axis, so its gravity term is zero. Everything it needs is inertia.
